import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conway's thrackle conjecture

A thrackle is a drawing of a finite simple graph in the plane by Jordan arcs such that every
pair of edges meets exactly once, at their common endpoint if they are adjacent and at a proper
crossing otherwise. Conway conjectured that a thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, Conway's thrackle conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway%27s_thrackle_conjecture)
-/

namespace ConwaysThrackleConjecture

/-- Two arcs have a proper crossing at `p` if, in a neighborhood of `p`, a topological change of
coordinates takes their images to the two coordinate axes. -/
def ProperCrossing (f g : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 → ℝ × ℝ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ U : Set (ℝ × ℝ), IsOpen U ∧ ∃ hp : p ∈ U, ∃ h : U → ℝ × ℝ,
    Topology.IsOpenEmbedding h ∧ h ⟨p, hp⟩ = (0, 0) ∧
      ∀ (q : ℝ × ℝ) (hq : q ∈ U),
        (q ∈ Set.range f ↔ (h ⟨q, hq⟩).2 = 0) ∧
          (q ∈ Set.range g ↔ (h ⟨q, hq⟩).1 = 0)

/-- The points in the interior of an arc parametrized by `[0,1]`. -/
def interiorRange (f : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 → ℝ × ℝ) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | ∃ t : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, 0 < (t : ℝ) ∧ (t : ℝ) < 1 ∧ f t = p}

/-- A thrackle drawing of a simple graph in the plane. Edges are injective continuous arcs.
Adjacent edges meet only at their common endpoint. Non-adjacent edges meet at one proper
interior crossing. -/
structure ThrackleDrawing {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  vertex : V → ℝ × ℝ
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  edge : G.edgeSet → C(Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ℝ × ℝ)
  edge_injective : ∀ e, Function.Injective (edge e)
  edge_endpoints : ∀ e,
    ({edge e ⟨0, by norm_num⟩, edge e ⟨1, by norm_num⟩} : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) =
      {p | ∃ v, v ∈ e.1 ∧ p = vertex v}
  avoids_other_vertices : ∀ e v, vertex v ∈ Set.range (edge e) ↔ v ∈ e.1
  adjacent_edge_intersections : ∀ e f, e ≠ f → (∃ v, v ∈ e.1 ∧ v ∈ f.1) →
    Set.range (edge e) ∩ Set.range (edge f) =
      vertex '' {v | v ∈ e.1 ∧ v ∈ f.1}
  nonadjacent_edge_intersections : ∀ e f, e ≠ f → (¬ ∃ v, v ∈ e.1 ∧ v ∈ f.1) →
    ∃ p, Set.range (edge e) ∩ Set.range (edge f) = {p} ∧
      p ∈ interiorRange (edge e) ∧ p ∈ interiorRange (edge f) ∧
      ProperCrossing (edge e) (edge f) p

/-- **Conway's thrackle conjecture.** Every finite simple graph admitting a thrackle drawing in
the plane has at most as many edges as vertices. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 57]
theorem conways_thrackle_conjecture :
    ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      Nonempty (ThrackleDrawing G) → G.edgeFinset.card ≤ Fintype.card V := by
  sorry

end ConwaysThrackleConjecture
modeling_decisions: Interpreted the terse list-page entry using the linked Wikipedia article and the supplied decomposition: a thrackle is a drawing of a finite simple graph in the real plane whose edges are Jordan arcs, with each pair of distinct edges meeting exactly once.

Represented a finite simple graph by `SimpleGraph V` with `Fintype V`; the theorem quantifies over all such graphs and says that existence (`Nonempty`) of a thrackle drawing implies `G.edgeFinset.card ≤ Fintype.card V`. Isolated vertices are allowed, as in the graph-theoretic statement.

Represented each Jordan arc by a continuous map from the closed unit interval into `ℝ × ℝ`, together with injectivity. Its two endpoint images are required to be exactly the two incident vertex positions, and arcs are forbidden from passing through any other represented vertex.

For distinct adjacent edges, required the intersection of their full images to equal exactly the image of their common vertex set. For distinct non-adjacent edges, required the full image intersection to be a singleton lying in the interiors of both arcs.

Modeled a transverse/proper crossing topologically rather than differentiably, because the source assumes arbitrary Jordan arcs: on an open neighborhood of the crossing, an open topological embedding gives coordinates in which the two arc images are the two coordinate axes.

/-- Two parametrized arcs cross transversely at interior parameters `t` and `u` if an ambient
homeomorphism of the plane locally sends their germs to the two coordinate axes, with the two
sides of each parameter sent to the two corresponding half-axes. -/
def TransverseAt (f g : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 → ℝ × ℝ)
    (t u : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) : Prop :=
  (t : ℝ) ∈ Ioo 0 1 ∧ (u : ℝ) ∈ Ioo 0 1 ∧ f t = g u ∧
    ∃ h : (ℝ × ℝ) ≃ₜ (ℝ × ℝ), ∃ ε > 0, ∃ δ > 0,
      h (f t) = (0, 0) ∧
      (∀ s, Dist.dist s t < ε →
        (h (f s)).2 = 0 ∧
          (s = t ∨ 0 < (h (f s)).1 * ((s : ℝ) - (t : ℝ)))) ∧
      (∀ s, Dist.dist s u < δ →
        (h (g s)).1 = 0 ∧
          (s = u ∨ 0 < (h (g s)).2 * ((s : ℝ) - (u : ℝ))))

/-- A thrackle drawing of a simple graph. Vertices are distinct points of the plane. Every
edge is a Jordan arc between its endpoints and avoids all other vertices. Distinct adjacent edges
meet only at their common endpoint, while distinct non-adjacent edges have exactly one point in
common, where they cross transversely in their interiors. -/

  vertex : V → ℝ × ℝ
  edge : G.edgeSet → Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 → ℝ × ℝ
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  edge_continuous : ∀ e : G.edgeSet, Continuous (edge e)
  edge_injective : ∀ e : G.edgeSet, Function.Injective (edge e)
  edge_endpoints : ∀ e : G.edgeSet, ∃ v w, (e : Sym2 V) = s(v, w) ∧
    edge e 0 = vertex v ∧ edge e 1 = vertex w
  edge_avoids_vertices : ∀ (e : G.edgeSet) v,
    vertex v ∈ range (edge e) ↔ v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)
  adjacent_edge_intersections : ∀ (e f : G.edgeSet), e ≠ f →
    (∃ v, v ∈ (e : Sym2 V) ∧ v ∈ (f : Sym2 V)) →
      range (edge e) ∩ range (edge f) =
        {p | ∃ v, v ∈ (e : Sym2 V) ∧ v ∈ (f : Sym2 V) ∧ p = vertex v}
  nonadjacent_edge_intersections : ∀ (e f : G.edgeSet), e ≠ f →
    (¬ ∃ v, v ∈ (e : Sym2 V) ∧ v ∈ (f : Sym2 V)) →
      ∃ t u, TransverseAt (edge e) (edge f) t u ∧
        range (edge e) ∩ range (edge f) = {edge e t}

  Nonempty (ThrackleDrawing G)

plane has at most as many edges as vertices. -/

/-!
# Conway's thrackle conjecture

A *thrackle* is a drawing of a finite simple graph in the plane such that the vertices are
distinct points, each edge is a Jordan arc joining the points of its two endpoints, and every
pair of distinct edges meets exactly once. Two edges with a common endpoint may meet only at that
endpoint. Two edges with no common endpoint meet at exactly one point, which is interior to both
arcs, and they must cross transversally there (a tangency is not allowed).

Conway conjectured that a thrackle cannot have more edges than vertices.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Conway's thrackle conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway%27s_thrackle_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [FP11] Fulek, R. and Pach, J., _A computational approach to Conway's thrackle conjecture_.
  European Journal of Combinatorics 32 (2011), 1281–1291.
  [arXiv:1002.3904](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.3904)
- [FP17] Fulek, R. and Pach, J., _Thrackles: An Improved Upper Bound_.
  [arXiv:1708.08037](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08037)
-/

namespace ConwaysThrackleConjecture

open Set Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry unitInterval

/-- The curve `δ` *properly crosses* the curve `γ` at time `t`: the point `δ t` lies on `γ`,
the time `t` is interior, and there is a neighbourhood `U` of `δ t` such that, shortly before and
shortly after time `t`, the curve `δ` avoids `γ` and lies in two different connected components
of `U \ range γ`. In other words, at the point `δ t` the curve `δ` passes from one side of `γ`
to its other side, as opposed to touching `γ` and staying on the same side. -/
def ProperlyCrossesAt (γ δ : I → ℝ²) (t : I) : Prop :=
  δ t ∈ range γ ∧ 0 < t ∧ t < 1 ∧
    ∃ U ∈ 𝓝 (δ t), ∃ η > 0, ∀ t₁ t₂ : I,
      (t : ℝ) - η < t₁ → t₁ < t → t < t₂ → (t₂ : ℝ) < t + η →
        δ t₁ ∈ U \ range γ ∧ δ t₂ ∈ U \ range γ ∧
          connectedComponentIn (U \ range γ) (δ t₁) ≠
            connectedComponentIn (U \ range γ) (δ t₂)

variable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)

/-- A *drawing* of the simple graph `G` in the plane (a *topological graph*): the vertices are
drawn as distinct points, each edge `e = {u, v}` is drawn as a Jordan arc (a continuous injective
curve parametrised by `[0, 1]`) with endpoints the points of `u` and `v`, and no arc passes through
the point of a vertex other than its own endpoints. -/
structure Drawing where
  /-- The point of the plane representing the vertex `v`. -/
  vertex : V → ℝ²
  /-- The arc representing the edge `e`, parametrised by the unit interval. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → I → ℝ²
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  continuous_arc (e : G.edgeSet) : Continuous (arc e)
  arc_injective (e : G.edgeSet) : Function.Injective (arc e)
  arc_endpoints (e : G.edgeSet) : s(arc e 0, arc e 1) = Sym2.map vertex e
  arc_vertex (e : G.edgeSet) (t : I) (v : V) : arc e t = vertex v → v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)

variable {G}

/-- A drawing of `G` is a *thrackle* if every two distinct edges meet exactly once. Two edges
with a common endpoint therefore meet only at that endpoint. Two edges with no common endpoint
meet at exactly one point, and at this point each of them properly crosses the other. -/
def Drawing.IsThrackle (D : Drawing G) : Prop :=
  ∀ e₁ e₂ : G.edgeSet, e₁ ≠ e₂ →
    (∃! p, p ∈ range (D.arc e₁) ∩ range (D.arc e₂)) ∧
    ((∀ v, v ∈ (e₁ : Sym2 V) → v ∉ (e₂ : Sym2 V)) →
      ∀ t, D.arc e₂ t ∈ range (D.arc e₁) → ProperlyCrossesAt (D.arc e₁) (D.arc e₂) t)

/-- **Conway's thrackle conjecture.** Thrackles cannot have more edges than vertices: if a finite
simple graph `G` admits a thrackle drawing in the plane, then the number of edges of `G` is at
most the number of vertices of `G`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem conways_thrackle_conjecture [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (D : Drawing G) (hD : D.IsThrackle) : G.edgeFinset.card ≤ Fintype.card V := by
  sorry

/-- Every drawing of a graph without edges is a thrackle. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem Drawing.isThrackle_bot (D : Drawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V)) : D.IsThrackle :=
  fun e => absurd e.2 (by simp)

/-- The only edge of the complete graph on two vertices is `s(0, 1)`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
private lemma coe_edge_top_fin_two (e : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).edgeSet) :
    (e : Sym2 (Fin 2)) = s(0, 1) := by
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := e
  induction e using Sym2.ind with
  | h a b =>
    simp only [SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet, SimpleGraph.top_adj] at he
    fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> simp_all [Sym2.eq_swap]

/-- The straight-line drawing of a single edge as the segment from `(0, 0)` to `(1, 0)`. -/
noncomputable def segmentDrawing : Drawing (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) where
  vertex i := (i : ℝ) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1
  arc _ t := (t : ℝ) • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1
  vertex_injective i j h :=
    Fin.ext (by exact_mod_cast smul_left_injective ℝ (EuclideanSpace.single_eq_zero_iff.not.2
      one_ne_zero) h)
  continuous_arc _ := by fun_prop
  arc_injective _ t₁ t₂ h :=
    Subtype.ext (smul_left_injective ℝ (EuclideanSpace.single_eq_zero_iff.not.2 one_ne_zero) h)
  arc_endpoints e := by
    rw [coe_edge_top_fin_two e]
    simp
  arc_vertex e t v _ := by
    rw [coe_edge_top_fin_two e, Sym2.mem_iff]
    omega

/-- A single straight segment is a thrackle. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem segmentDrawing_isThrackle : segmentDrawing.IsThrackle := fun e₁ e₂ h =>
  absurd (Subtype.ext ((coe_edge_top_fin_two e₁).trans (coe_edge_top_fin_two e₂).symm)) h

end ConwaysThrackleConjecture

namespace ConwaysThrackleConjecture

open Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/-- The arc `α` (parametrised by `[0, 1]`) *properly crosses* the arc `β` (parametrised by
`[0, 1]`) at the parameter `s`: the point `α s` is an interior point of `α` and, near `α s`,
`α` passes from one side of `β` to the other side. Concretely, there is a neighbourhood `U` of
`α s` and an `ε > 0` such that for every `u ∈ (0, ε]` the points `α (s - u)` and `α (s + u)`
lie in `U` and cannot be joined by a path inside `U` avoiding `β`.

For two Jordan arcs `α` and `β` that meet only at the point `α s`, this says exactly that the
two half-arcs of `α` at `α s` lie locally on different sides of `β`, so that `α` and `β` cross
at `α s` rather than merely touch there. -/
def CrossesAt (α β : ℝ → ℝ²) (s : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ U ∈ 𝓝 (α s), ∃ ε > 0, Set.Icc (s - ε) (s + ε) ⊆ Set.Icc 0 1 ∧
    ∀ u ∈ Set.Ioc 0 ε, α (s - u) ∈ U ∧ α (s + u) ∈ U ∧
      ¬ JoinedIn (U \ β '' Set.Icc 0 1) (α (s - u)) (α (s + u))

/-- `IsThrackle G pos arc` says that the map `pos` on vertices and the family `arc` of curves
(parametrised by `[0, 1]`) indexed by the edges of `G` form a *thrackle drawing* of the simple
graph `G` in the plane:
* distinct vertices are drawn as distinct points;
* every edge is drawn as a Jordan arc (an injective continuous curve) whose two endpoints are
  the points representing the two endpoints of the edge;
* no arc passes through the point representing a vertex other than its own endpoints;
* every two distinct edges meet in exactly one point;
* every two edges without a common endpoint properly cross at their meeting point.

Two edges with a common endpoint meet exactly once, so they meet only at that common endpoint.
Two edges without a common endpoint meet at a point that is interior to both arcs, since the
endpoints of an arc are vertices, which the other arc avoids. -/
structure IsThrackle {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (pos : V → ℝ²)
    (arc : G.edgeSet → ℝ → ℝ²) : Prop where
  pos_injective : Function.Injective pos
  continuousOn (e : G.edgeSet) : ContinuousOn (arc e) (Set.Icc 0 1)
  injOn (e : G.edgeSet) : Set.InjOn (arc e) (Set.Icc 0 1)
  endpoints (e : G.edgeSet) : s(arc e 0, arc e 1) = (e : Sym2 V).map pos
  avoids_vertices (e : G.edgeSet) (v : V) : pos v ∈ arc e '' Set.Icc 0 1 → v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)
  meet_once (e f : G.edgeSet) : e ≠ f →
    ∃ p, arc e '' Set.Icc 0 1 ∩ arc f '' Set.Icc 0 1 = {p}
  crosses (e f : G.edgeSet) : (∀ v ∈ (e : Sym2 V), v ∉ (f : Sym2 V)) →
    ∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 1, ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1, arc e s = arc f t → CrossesAt (arc e) (arc f) s

/-- **Conway's thrackle conjecture.** A thrackle cannot have more edges than vertices: if a
finite simple graph `G` admits a thrackle drawing in the plane, then the number of edges of `G`
is at most the number of vertices of `G`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem conways_thrackle_conjecture {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (pos : V → ℝ²) (arc : G.edgeSet → ℝ → ℝ²)
    (h : IsThrackle G pos arc) : G.edgeFinset.card ≤ Fintype.card V := by
  sorry

/-- A graph without edges is a thrackle for any injective placement of its vertices. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem isThrackle_bot {V : Type*} (pos : V → ℝ²) (hpos : Function.Injective pos)
    (arc : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).edgeSet → ℝ → ℝ²) : IsThrackle ⊥ pos arc where
  pos_injective := hpos
  continuousOn e := (SimpleGraph.edgeSet_bot.subset e.2).elim
  injOn e := (SimpleGraph.edgeSet_bot.subset e.2).elim
  endpoints e := (SimpleGraph.edgeSet_bot.subset e.2).elim
  avoids_vertices e := (SimpleGraph.edgeSet_bot.subset e.2).elim
  meet_once e := (SimpleGraph.edgeSet_bot.subset e.2).elim
  crosses e := (SimpleGraph.edgeSet_bot.subset e.2).elim

/-- Two perpendicular straight segments properly cross at their common midpoint. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem crossesAt_perpendicular_segments :
    CrossesAt (fun t => !₂[2 * t - 1, 0]) (fun t => !₂[0, 2 * t - 1]) (1 / 2) := by
  refine ⟨{p | p 1 ∈ Set.Ioo (-1) 1}, ?_, 1 / 2, by norm_num, by norm_num, ?_⟩
  · refine (isOpen_Ioo.preimage (EuclideanSpace.proj (1 : Fin 2)).continuous).mem_nhds ?_
    simp
  · intro u hu
    refine ⟨by simp, by simp, ?_⟩
    rintro ⟨γ, hγ⟩
    have hf : Continuous fun t : unitInterval => γ t 0 :=
      (EuclideanSpace.proj (0 : Fin 2)).continuous.comp γ.continuous
    have h0 : (0 : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc (γ 0 0) (γ 1 0) := by
      simp only [Path.source, Path.target]
      constructor <;> simp <;> linarith [hu.1]
    obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := intermediate_value_univ 0 1 hf h0
    obtain ⟨hU, hβ⟩ := hγ t
    apply hβ
    refine ⟨(γ t 1 + 1) / 2, ⟨by linarith [hU.1], by linarith [hU.2]⟩, ?_⟩
    ext i
    fin_cases i
    · simpa using ht.symm
    · simp; ring

end ConwaysThrackleConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conway's thrackle conjecture

A *thrackle* is a drawing of a finite simple graph in the plane in which the vertices are
represented by distinct points, each edge is represented by a Jordan arc joining the points of its
two endpoints and avoiding the points of all other vertices, and every two edges meet exactly once.
Two edges with a common endpoint meet only at that endpoint. Two edges with no common endpoint meet
at exactly one point of their interiors, where they must cross properly (transversally): they may
not merely touch.

Conway's thrackle conjecture asserts that a thrackle cannot have more edges than vertices.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Conway's thrackle conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway%27s_thrackle_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [LPS97] L. Lovász, J. Pach, M. Szegedy, *On Conway's thrackle conjecture*,
  Discrete Comput. Geom. 18 (1997), 369–376.
- [FP19] R. Fulek, J. Pach, *Thrackles: An improved upper bound*,
  Discrete Appl. Math. 259 (2019), 226–231. [arXiv:1708.08037](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08037)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace ConwaysThrackleConjecture

/-- A set `A` in the plane is a *Jordan arc* from `a` to `b` if it is the image of an injective
path from `a` to `b`, i.e. of a topological embedding of the unit interval sending `0` to `a` and
`1` to `b`. -/
def IsJordanArc (A : Set ℝ²) (a b : ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ γ : Path a b, Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = A

/-- Two subsets `A` and `B` of the plane *cross properly* at a point `p` if, near `p`, the pair
`(A, B)` looks like the pair of coordinate axes near the origin. That is, there is a homeomorphism
`φ` from an open neighbourhood of `p` onto an open neighbourhood of `0` that sends `p` to `0`,
the part of `A` in its domain onto the part of the first coordinate axis in its image, and the
part of `B` in its domain onto the part of the second coordinate axis in its image.
In particular, at `p` the set `A` passes from one side of `B` to the other side; the two sets
do not merely touch at `p`. -/
def CrossesProperlyAt (A B : Set ℝ²) (p : ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph ℝ² ℝ², p ∈ φ.source ∧ φ p = 0 ∧
    φ '' (A ∩ φ.source) = φ.target ∩ {x | x 1 = 0} ∧
    φ '' (B ∩ φ.source) = φ.target ∩ {x | x 0 = 0}

variable {V : Type*}

/-- A *drawing* of a simple graph `G` in the plane. The vertices are represented by distinct
points, and each edge `s(u, v)` is represented by a Jordan arc from the point of `u` to the point
of `v` that does not pass through the point of any other vertex. Edges are allowed to cross. -/
structure Drawing (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  /-- The point representing a vertex. -/
  vertex : V → ℝ²
  /-- The arc representing an edge. -/
  edge : G.edgeSet → Set ℝ²
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  isJordanArc_edge : ∀ u v (h : G.Adj u v),
    IsJordanArc (edge ⟨s(u, v), h⟩) (vertex u) (vertex v)
  vertex_notMem_edge : ∀ (e : G.edgeSet) (w : V), w ∉ (e : Sym2 V) → vertex w ∉ edge e

variable {G : SimpleGraph V}

/-- A drawing of `G` is a *thrackle* if every two distinct edges meet exactly once, and two edges
with no endpoint in common cross properly at their meeting point.

Two edges with a common endpoint both contain the point of that endpoint, so they meet exactly
there. Two edges with no common endpoint meet at a point that is not the point of a vertex, so it
is an interior point of both arcs. -/
structure Drawing.IsThrackle (D : Drawing G) : Prop where
  inter_eq_singleton : ∀ e f : G.edgeSet, e ≠ f → ∃ p, D.edge e ∩ D.edge f = {p}
  crossesProperlyAt : ∀ e f : G.edgeSet, (∀ w ∈ (e : Sym2 V), w ∉ (f : Sym2 V)) →
    ∀ p ∈ D.edge e ∩ D.edge f, CrossesProperlyAt (D.edge e) (D.edge f) p

/-- The point of an endpoint of an edge lies on the arc representing the edge. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem Drawing.vertex_mem_edge (D : Drawing G) (e : G.edgeSet) {w : V} (hw : w ∈ (e : Sym2 V)) :
    D.vertex w ∈ D.edge e := by
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := e
  induction e using Sym2.ind with
  | _ u v =>
    obtain ⟨γ, -, hγ⟩ := D.isJordanArc_edge u v he
    rw [Sym2.mem_iff] at hw
    rcases hw with rfl | rfl
    · exact hγ ▸ ⟨0, γ.source⟩
    · exact hγ ▸ ⟨1, γ.target⟩

/-- In a thrackle, two distinct edges with a common endpoint meet exactly at the point of that
endpoint. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem Drawing.IsThrackle.inter_eq_singleton_vertex {D : Drawing G} (hD : D.IsThrackle)
    {e f : G.edgeSet} (hef : e ≠ f) {w : V} (hwe : w ∈ (e : Sym2 V))
    (hwf : w ∈ (f : Sym2 V)) :
    D.edge e ∩ D.edge f = {D.vertex w} := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hD.inter_eq_singleton e f hef
  have : D.vertex w ∈ D.edge e ∩ D.edge f :=
    ⟨D.vertex_mem_edge e hwe, D.vertex_mem_edge f hwf⟩
  rw [hp] at this ⊢
  rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp this]

/-- **Conway's thrackle conjecture.** Thrackles cannot have more edges than vertices: if a finite
simple graph $G$ admits a drawing in the plane that is a thrackle, then $|E(G)| \le |V(G)|$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem conways_thrackle_conjecture [Fintype V] [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (D : Drawing G) (hD : D.IsThrackle) :
    G.edgeFinset.card ≤ Fintype.card V := by
  sorry

/-- The two coordinate axes cross properly at the origin. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem crossesProperlyAt_axes :
    CrossesProperlyAt {x : ℝ² | x 1 = 0} {x : ℝ² | x 0 = 0} 0 :=
  ⟨OpenPartialHomeomorph.refl ℝ², by simp, by simp, by simp, by simp⟩

/-- A straight line segment between two distinct points is a Jordan arc. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
theorem isJordanArc_segment {a b : ℝ²} (hab : a ≠ b) : IsJordanArc (segment ℝ a b) a b := by
  refine ⟨⟨⟨fun t => AffineMap.lineMap a b (t : ℝ), by fun_prop⟩, by simp, by simp⟩,
    ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro s t hst
    exact Subtype.ext (AffineMap.lineMap_injective ℝ hab hst)
  · rw [segment_eq_image_lineMap]
    ext x
    simp only [Set.mem_range, Set.mem_image, Set.mem_Icc]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨t, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨t, ⟨t.2.1, t.2.2⟩, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, rfl⟩

/-- The drawing of the graph with a single edge as a straight segment. -/
noncomputable def segmentDrawing : Drawing (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) where
  vertex i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1
  edge _ := segment ℝ (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1)
  vertex_injective i j h := by simpa using congrFun (congrArg (⇑) h) i
  isJordanArc_edge u v h := by
    have hne :
        (EuclideanSpace.single (0 : Fin 2) (1 : ℝ) : ℝ²) ≠ EuclideanSpace.single 1 1 := by
      intro h
      simpa using congrFun (congrArg (⇑) h) 0
    fin_cases u <;> fin_cases v
    · simp at h
    · exact isJordanArc_segment hne
    · simpa [segment_symm] using isJordanArc_segment hne.symm
    · simp at h
  vertex_notMem_edge e w hw := by
    obtain ⟨⟨x, y⟩, hxy⟩ := e
    have : x ≠ y := hxy
    exfalso
    apply hw
    fin_cases w <;> fin_cases x <;> fin_cases y <;> simp_all

/-- The drawing of a single edge as a straight segment is a thrackle. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem segmentDrawing_isThrackle : segmentDrawing.IsThrackle where
  inter_eq_singleton e f hef := by
    exfalso
    apply hef
    obtain ⟨⟨x, y⟩, hxy⟩ := e
    obtain ⟨⟨x', y'⟩, hxy'⟩ := f
    have : x ≠ y := hxy
    have : x' ≠ y' := hxy'
    fin_cases x <;> fin_cases y <;> fin_cases x' <;> fin_cases y' <;> simp_all [Sym2.eq_swap]
  crossesProperlyAt e f hef p hp := by
    exfalso
    obtain ⟨⟨x, y⟩, hxy⟩ := e
    obtain ⟨⟨x', y'⟩, hxy'⟩ := f
    have : x ≠ y := hxy
    have : x' ≠ y' := hxy'
    fin_cases x <;> fin_cases y <;> fin_cases x' <;> fin_cases y' <;> simp_all

end ConwaysThrackleConjecture

modeling_decisions: Graphs are finite simple graphs `SimpleGraph V` with `[Fintype V]`; the count uses `G.edgeFinset.card` (needs `[DecidableRel G.Adj]`) vs `Fintype.card V`. Loops/parallel edges are excluded by `SimpleGraph`, consistent with the literature (parallel edges would meet twice).

A drawing assigns distinct points to vertices (`vertex_injective`), and to each edge of `G.edgeSet` a set that is a Jordan arc from the point of one endpoint to the point of the other (`IsJordanArc` = range of an injective `Path`; injective + compact domain ⇒ topological embedding) and that contains no point of a non-incident vertex (`vertex_notMem_edge`). The edge field is indexed by `G.edgeSet`, and the arc condition is imposed for both orderings (u,v),(v,u) of an edge, which is consistent since `s(u,v)=s(v,u)`.

`IsThrackle` = (i) every two distinct edges meet in exactly one point (`∃ p, edge e ∩ edge f = {p}`), and (ii) two edges with no common vertex cross properly at every (hence the unique) common point. The Wikipedia clause 'adjacent edges meet only at their common endpoint' is a consequence (both arcs contain the vertex point and the intersection is a singleton) — proved in the file as `Drawing.IsThrackle.inter_eq_singleton_vertex`. 'Interior point' for non-adjacent edges is also a consequence of `vertex_notMem_edge` + injectivity, so it is not restated.

Transversality ('proper crossing') for general Jordan arcs is defined topologically: `CrossesProperlyAt A B p` holds iff there is an `OpenPartialHomeomorph ℝ² ℝ²` defined on a neighbourhood of p, sending p to 0, A∩source onto (target ∩ first coordinate axis) and B∩source onto (target ∩ second coordinate axis). This is the standard local model of two arcs crossing (branches alternate around p); a touching/tangency (e.g. x-axis and parabola y=x²) is excluded because a complementary region bounded by two branches of the same arc is a homeomorphism invariant. Equivalence with the informal 'one arc passes from one side of the other to the other side' for arcs meeting exactly once relies on the tameness of finite graphs embedded in the plane; in any case the class of thrackleable graphs is known to be insensitive to the regularity class of the arcs. Transversality is essential (it is not an artifact): with tangencies allowed, 'tangled thrackles' with more edges than vertices exist. Reviewers should check this definition.

Transversality is required only for edges with no common endpoint (as in Wikipedia), not for adjacent edges at their common vertex; Conway's original 'distinct tangents' phrasing for smooth curves would also constrain the vertex, but this does not change which graphs are thrackleable.
Three or more edges passing through a common crossing point are not forbidden (Wikipedia does not forbid this and it does not affect the conjecture).
Statement is a universally quantified inequality with hypotheses `(D : Drawing G) (hD : D.IsThrackle)` rather than `(∃ D, D.IsThrackle) →`; these are equivalent.

points on both sides of that axis in every neighborhood of `x`. -/

  (∃ s : unitInterval, s ≠ 0 ∧ s ≠ 1 ∧ γ s = x) ∧
  (∃ t : unitInterval, t ≠ 0 ∧ t ≠ 1 ∧ δ t = x) ∧
  ∃ h : OpenPartialHomeomorph Plane Plane,

    ∀ U : Set Plane, IsOpen U → x ∈ U →

A *thrackle* is a drawing of a finite simple graph in the plane in which the vertices are
distinct points, each edge is a Jordan arc (a simple continuous curve) joining the points of its
two endpoints and passing through no other vertex, and every pair of distinct edges meets exactly

common endpoint meet at exactly one point of their interiors, where they must cross properly
(transversally), i.e. one curve passes from one side of the other curve to its other side.

John H. Conway conjectured that every thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Conway's thrackle conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway%27s_thrackle_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [LPS97] Lovász, L., Pach, J., Szegedy, M., _On Conway's thrackle conjecture_.
  Discrete Comput. Geom. 18 (1997), 369–376.
- [FP11] Fulek, R., Pach, J., _A computational approach to Conway's thrackle conjecture_.
  Comput. Geom. 44 (2011), 345–355. [arXiv:1002.3904](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.3904)
- [FP19] Fulek, R., Pach, J., _Thrackles: An improved upper bound_.
  Discrete Appl. Math. 259 (2019), 226–231. [arXiv:1708.08037](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08037)

namespace ConwaysThrackleConjecture

open Topology
open scoped unitInterval EuclideanGeometry

/--
The curve `δ : I → ℝ²` **crosses** the curve `γ : I → ℝ²` at the interior parameter `s₀` if
the point `δ s₀` lies on `γ` and, in some neighbourhood `U` of `δ s₀`, the points of `δ` just
before `s₀` and just after `s₀` lie on different sides of `γ`: they cannot be joined by a path
inside `U` that avoids `γ`. This is the informal condition that `δ` passes from one side of `γ`
to its other side at `δ s₀`, as opposed to touching `γ` tangentially.
-/
def CrossesAt (γ δ : I → ℝ²) (s₀ : I) : Prop :=
  0 < s₀ ∧ s₀ < 1 ∧ δ s₀ ∈ Set.range γ ∧
    ∃ U ∈ 𝓝 (δ s₀), ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[<] s₀, ∀ᶠ s' in 𝓝[>] s₀,
      ¬ JoinedIn (U \ Set.range γ) (δ s) (δ s')

/--
Two curves `γ δ : I → ℝ²` have a **proper crossing** at the point `p` if `p` is an interior
point of both curves and each curve crosses the other at `p`, i.e. the four half-curves emanating
from `p` alternate around `p`. This is the transversality condition in the definition of a
thrackle.
-/
def IsProperCrossing (γ δ : I → ℝ²) (p : ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ t₀ s₀ : I, γ t₀ = p ∧ δ s₀ = p ∧ CrossesAt γ δ s₀ ∧ CrossesAt δ γ t₀

vertex `v` and a curve `arc e : I → ℝ²` for each edge `e` such that:
- distinct vertices are drawn as distinct points;
- each edge is drawn as a Jordan arc (a continuous injective curve) whose two endpoints are the
  points representing the two ends of the edge;
- no arc passes through a vertex other than its endpoints;
- every two distinct edges meet in exactly one point (so two edges with a common endpoint
  meet only at that endpoint);
- two edges with no common endpoint cross properly (transversally) at their meeting point.
-/

attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is appropriate; the 'every thrackle is a pseudoforest' reformulation and the known partial bounds are not part of the list-page statement and were not posed.
modeling_decisions: The list-page statement is terse; the definition of 'thrackle' was taken from the Wikipedia article and the cited papers (Fulek–Pach): a drawing of a finite simple graph with vertices as distinct points, edges as Jordan arcs not passing through other vertices, every pair of edges meeting exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper (transverse) crossing.

Graphs are finite simple graphs: `SimpleGraph V` with `[Fintype V]`; the conclusion is `G.edgeSet.ncard ≤ Fintype.card V` (non-strict, 'cannot have more edges than vertices'). The theorem quantifies over graphs together with a thrackle drawing, which is equivalent to 'every thrackle(able graph) has at most as many edges as vertices'.

Edges are indexed by `G.edgeSet` (unordered `Sym2`), so the endpoint condition is `s(arc e 0, arc e 1) = e.map vertex`. Jordan arcs are `I → ℝ²` maps that are continuous and injective (equivalent to embeddings since I is compact).

'Every pair of edges meets exactly once' is `∀ e ≠ e', ∃ p, range (arc e) ∩ range (arc e') = {p}`. Together with `endpoints`/`avoids_vertices`, this forces adjacent edges to meet only at their common vertex and forces the meeting point of vertex-disjoint edges to be interior to both arcs; no separate axiom is needed for these.

Transversality ('one curve passes from one side of the other to its other side') is formalised topologically by `CrossesAt`: in some neighbourhood U of the meeting point, the points of δ just before and just after the meeting parameter are not path-connected in U \ range γ. Since every arc in ℝ² is locally flat (tame), this is equivalent to the chart-based informal notion; a tangential touching is never a CrossesAt, and a genuine transverse crossing always is. The requirement is imposed symmetrically (`IsProperCrossing` = each arc crosses the other), which is harmless (the two directions are equivalent for arcs meeting once) and matches the symmetric word 'transverse'. Reviewers should check this definition, as it is the main subtle point.

Tests included: perpendicular segments form an IsProperCrossing; a V-shaped curve touching the axis is not a CrossesAt (non-vacuity of transversality); the single-edge graph drawn as a segment is an IsThrackleDrawing.
